title: Boolean machine for an iteration body
statement: Let $E$ and $G$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, with $k_E$ and $k_G$ work tapes, and assume $k_E>0$. Choose states $e_e,e_x$ of $E$ and $g_e,g_x$ of $G$. The constructed machine has $�max(k_E,k_G)$ work tapes and a state set that includes copying, rewind, input-return, anchoring, and the states used to simulate $E$ and $G$. It copies the input symbols onto work tape $0$, rewinds that tape to its first blank cell, moves the input head back to its left blank cell, then simulates $E$ from $e_e$ at the anchor; on reaching $e_x$ it starts $G$ from $g_e$, and on reaching $g_x$ it returns to the anchor. Each simulation uses the corresponding machine's work tapes, with extra tapes stationary, and returns to its call state unless its current state is the designated exit state.
hypotheses_covered: $E$ has a positive number of work tapes
